title: 5 PC game deals worth buying this week
metaDescription: Five genuinely good PC games at genuinely good prices in the July 29 snapshot, each with the evidence behind it and the catch you should know first.
socialDescription: Five PC game deals where the price and the player reviews both actually hold up this week.
socialSummary: Disco Elysium, Red Dead Redemption 2, Slay the Spire and two more, all properly cheap right now.
intro: There are hundreds of discounted games in the latest LootRadar snapshot and most of them do not deserve a second of your time. These five clawed their way to the top because the price is backed by an enormous pile of positive player reviews, rather than by a percentage someone made large on purpose.

Treat it as a starting point, not a shopping list. Take the one that matches what you actually feel like playing, check the edition and activation details, and walk away from the other four with a completely clear conscience.

picks.title: Disco Elysium - The Final Cut
picks.imageAlt: Disco Elysium - The Final Cut cover art
picks.copy: 92% positive across roughly 57,100 Steam reviews, which is a mountain of evidence for a reputation this big. There is no combat here. Your own skills argue with you inside your head, failing a check often produces the better scene, and the writing is some of the finest in the medium. At 78% off, if you have been meaning to get to it for years, this is the week.

picks.title: Red Dead Redemption 2
picks.copy: 92% positive from more than 307,000 Steam reviews, which is about as much agreement as the internet is capable of producing. The most detailed open world anyone has built, and also the slowest. Your horse takes its time and so does the story. Buy it for the eighty-hour campaign, not for a quick Saturday, and clear some drive space first.

picks.title: Mortal Kombat 11 Ultimate
picks.copy: Single digits for the Ultimate edition, sitting on an 88% positive rating from about 87,500 reviews. Gorgeous, brutal, and packed with more single-player content than fighting games usually bother with. Two things to check before you commit: whether the included roster is the one you wanted, and whether enough people are still online in your region.

picks.title: Slay the Spire
picks.copy: 97% positive from roughly 76,400 reviews. That is the highest rating on this list and it is not an accident. A single run takes an hour, and working out how cards, relics and enemy patterns actually fit together takes hundreds. At 75% off it is the easiest recommendation here, with one warning: you will not stop at one run.

picks.title: Hogwarts Legacy
picks.copy: An 85% cut with a 91% positive Steam rating from about 142,500 reviews behind it. This is the big cinematic castle-wandering option of the group, and the castle really is the star. Two practical notes: this one lives on the Epic Games Store, and it is hungry enough that you should check your storage and your GPU before clicking buy.
